name: Matrix-3D
description: Upstream mirror of Skywork's Matrix-3D v0.1: omnidirectional explorable 3D world generation. A three-stage GPU pipeline turns a text prompt or a single image into a panorama (FLUX.1 LoRA), the panorama plus a camera trajectory into a panoramic tour video (Wan2.1 / Wan2.2-5B LoRA conditioned on MoGe-depth warped renders), and the video into a 3D Gaussian scene (optimisation-based Pano_GS_Opt or feed-forward PanoLRM). In the universe it is a generative world model: it fabricates plausible scenes, so its outputs are synthetic and must never be registered as observed geometry. Exposed as CLI stages, generate.sh and a Gradio demo; checkpoints are pulled from Hugging Face.

capabilities.label: One-command world generation (generate.sh)
capabilities.description: Runs Step1 text-to-panorama, Step2 torchrun panorama-to-video at 720p, Step3 optimisation-based 3D scene extraction into output/example1. Edit the prompt/output_dir inside the script; ~1 hour for 720p on an A800.
capabilities.side_effects: hours of GPU compute; writes output dir
capabilities.cost: GPU hours (16-80 GB VRAM by stage)

capabilities.label: Download model checkpoints
capabilities.description: `python code/download_checkpoints.py` pulls Ruicheng/moge-vitl, Iceclear/StableSR and Skywork/Matrix-3D artefacts (text2panoimage_lora.safetensors, pano_video_gen_480p.ckpt, pano_video_gen_720p.bin, pano_video_gen_720p_5b.safetensors, pano_lrm_480p.pt) into ./checkpoints/{moge,StableSR,flux_lora,pano_lrm,Wan-AI/wan_lora}.
capabilities.side_effects: tens of GB downloaded from huggingface.co

capabilities.label: Step 1: text/image to panorama (panoramic_image_generation.py)
capabilities.description: `python code/panoramic_image_generation.py --mode t2p --prompt "..." --output_path DIR` or `--mode i2p --input_image_path img.jpg [--fov F]` plus --seed/--device. Writes DIR/pano_img.jpg (equirectangular) and DIR/prompt.txt. Externally produced panoramas can be dropped into the same layout to skip this stage.

capabilities.label: Step 2: panorama to panoramic tour video (torchrun)
capabilities.description: `torchrun --nproc_per_node N code/panoramic_image_to_video.py --inout_dir DIR --resolution 480|720 [--movement_mode straight|s_curve|l_curve|r_curve] [--angle deg] [--movement_range 0-0.8] [--json_path cams.json] [--seed] [--use_5b_model] [--enable_vram_management]`. Estimates depth with MoGe, warps the panorama along the trajectory into rendered_rgb.mp4 / rendered_mask.mp4 conditions, and generates DIR/pano_video.mp4 (960x480 or 1440x720, 81 frames) with the Wan video LoRA. Multi-GPU via xfuser.
capabilities.cost: GPU 12-60 GB VRAM; ~1 h at 720p on A800

capabilities.label: Step 3a: optimisation-based 3D scene extraction
capabilities.description: `python code/panoramic_video_to_3DScene.py --inout_dir DIR --resolution 480|720 [--device]`. Optionally super-resolves the video (VideoSR/StableSR), initialises Gaussians from panoramic frames and runs Pano_GS_Opt training (3000 iterations); copies point_cloud/iteration_3000/point_cloud.ply to DIR/generated_3dgs_opt.ply.

capabilities.label: Step 3b: feed-forward PanoLRM reconstruction (480p)
capabilities.description: `python code/panoramic_video_480p_to_3DScene_lrm.py --video_path pano.mp4 --pose_path cams.json --out_path DIR [--config_paths ...] [--ckpt_path pano_lrm_480p.pt] [--wan_model_path] [--sample_idx] [--device] [-v]`. Single forward pass of the panoramic large reconstruction model; writes a Gaussian .ply and rendered perspective videos. Needs ~80 GB VRAM.

capabilities.label: Generate a camera trajectory JSON
capabilities.description: `python code/generate_example_camera.py` writes test_cam_{front,back,left,right}.json: 81 4x4 world-to-camera matrices (OpenCV convention) as a JSON list, the format accepted by --json_path / --pose_path. Adapt the script for custom rails.

capabilities.label: Gradio demo web UI (app_matrix3d.py)
capabilities.description: `python code/app_matrix3d.py --max_gpus N` launches a Gradio app (demo.launch(share=True) creates a public gradio.live tunnel) chaining text->video->3D on one GPU (>=62 GB) or text/image->video->3D across N GPUs. Helpers in code/gradio_demo/{image_to_video,extract_3d_scene}.py.
capabilities.side_effects: opens a public share tunnel; runs GPU jobs on user request

capabilities.label: Working directory (inout_dir) contract
capabilities.description: Stage handoff by files in one directory: pano_img.jpg|png + prompt.txt (Step1 out / Step2 in) -> condition/rendered_rgb.mp4, rendered_mask.mp4, generated/generated.mp4, pano_video.mp4 (Step2 out) -> generated_3dgs_opt.ply (Step3 out). Third-party panoramas (e.g. HunyuanWorld) may be substituted at Step1's output.

capabilities.label: Camera trajectory JSON contract
capabilities.description: JSON list of 81 4x4 world-to-camera matrices in OpenCV format, translations in the depth-scaled units of the panorama (example rails travel 1000 units). Sample: data/test_cameras/test_cam_front.json and data/case1/sample_cam.json.

capabilities.label: Generated 3DGS scene output
capabilities.description: generated_3dgs_opt.ply (or the LRM .ply): standard 3D Gaussian Splatting PLY reconstructed from the panoramic video, loadable in generic splat viewers. Scene scale is relative to MoGe's monocular depth estimate, not metric.

capabilities.label: Model zoo (Hugging Face Skywork/Matrix-3D)
capabilities.description: Text2PanoImage LoRA (~16 GB VRAM), PanoVideoGen-480p (~40 GB / 15 GB low-VRAM), PanoVideoGen-720p (~60 GB / 19 GB), PanoVideoGen-720p-5B (~19 GB / 12 GB), PanoLRM-480p (~80 GB); plus third-party MoGe-ViT-L, StableSR and VEnhancer weights.

metadata.framework: PyTorch 2.7, DiffSynth-Studio (FLUX.1, Wan2.1/2.2), MoGe, nvdiffrast, gaussian-splatting, xfuser, Gradio

relations.description: Inferred from formats, not code: the generated Gaussian PLY scenes are the kind of asset LichtFeld Studio opens (scene.load_ply) for inspection, editing and re-export. No reference between the repositories.

resources.name: sample data
resources.description: example images, case1 sample video + poses, test camera rails

resources.name: vendored components
resources.description: in-tree copies of upstream projects used by the stages

environment.name: HF_TOKEN
environment.purpose: Hugging Face token for the gated FLUX.1 and Wan2.1 weights the three-stage pipeline downloads.

environment.name: VISIBLE_GPU_NUM
environment.purpose: How many GPUs the pipeline may use. A capacity setting, not a credential.

reference.spatial: Scene-local, non-metric coordinates scaled by monocular depth; panoramas are equirectangular; no GIS.
reference.temporal: 81-frame camera tour (video time); no calendar time.
open_questions: Is Matrix-3D meant to be a synthetic-scene source for training/testing other nodes (bim-state-transformer-engine, payload-render-engine) or an operator content tool? No caller is evidenced.
The Gradio demo publishes a public share link by default; the universe should disable share=True before any deployment.

corpus.holding: No corpus. It fabricates panoramic scenes and Gaussian worlds from a prompt or a single image.

COR-003.note: Every output names the stage and checkpoint that produced it, which is the only provenance a fabrication can carry.

COR-005.note: Its outputs are declared synthetic rather than offered as observation, which is the refusal a generative model owes.

COR-006.note: Generates scenes and admits nothing; downstream systems decide whether to register them.

COR-008.note: Holds no history: each run is a GPU pipeline from prompt to scene.

COR-010.note: It fabricates plausible scenes, so its outputs must never be registered as observed geometry.
